### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **7** package(s): `@objectstack/cloud-connection`, `@objectstack/core`, `@objectstack/platform-objects`, `@objectstack/plugin-auth`, `@objectstack/plugin-security`, `@objectstack/runtime`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **92** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **5** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/core/src/security/resolve-authz-context.batch-equivalence.golden.json`, `packages/spec/authorable-surface/identity.json`, `packages/spec/liveness/position.json`, …), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**63** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json ed1de8c2db206be39aebd012e6c47503263bbf80`.

⛔ **14** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **5** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/core/src/security/resolve-authz-context.batch-equivalence.golden.json`, `packages/spec/authorable-surface/identity.json`, `packages/spec/liveness/position.json`, …) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **2** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `organization_id (symbol, 33 pages)`, `organization_id (literal, 33 pages)`
- **18** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **154** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json ed1de8c2db206be39aebd012e6c47503263bbf80` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `e226019f5986b7ece21660abbe69d0b003e3c0f8` — the merge of head `23d3545e641ded76978eb351618d574609ca31fe` into base `ed1de8c2db206be39aebd012e6c47503263bbf80`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin e226019f5986b7ece21660abbe69d0b003e3c0f8 && git checkout e226019f5986b7ece21660abbe69d0b003e3c0f8
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin ed1de8c2db206be39aebd012e6c47503263bbf80 23d3545e641ded76978eb351618d574609ca31fe && git checkout -B drift-repro ed1de8c2db206be39aebd012e6c47503263bbf80 && git merge --no-ff 23d3545e641ded76978eb351618d574609ca31fe

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json ed1de8c2db206be39aebd012e6c47503263bbf80
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs ed1de8c2db206be39aebd012e6c47503263bbf80` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `83b54d84f170655ccec3fa3de8e628b2d6e8261b`
Local-runs: none

Reviewed read-only: card #15204 (body and all 36 comments, the stage-1 dev report 6101432403 included), PR #22723 (body, 115-file list, net diff against `main` at this head, +2,997 / −779 = 3,776 changed lines) and the 35 check-runs on the head. Stage 1 of the cutover plan (6094501866), claim 6095611212.

**Gate verdicts on the head, read at posting time.** Of the seven required contexts, five are `success` (`Lint & Repo Gates`, `TypeScript Type Check`, `Build Core`, `Temporal Conformance (live PG + MySQL)`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`) and **two are `failure`: `Test Core` and `Dogfood Regression Gate`**. The red shards: `Test Core (3/6)` fails on `packages/mcp` tests, `Test Core (4/6)` on `packages/cli` tests, `Test Core (5/6)` on `packages/metadata-protocol` tests, `Dogfood Regression Gate (1/3)` on `packages/qa/dogfood` (step "Boot example apps and exercise real user flows"), each `pnpm run test` exit 1. The failure text is not readable from this seat (the job-log and run-summary artifact fetches are refused at the storage redirect), so the shards' conclusions are the record. None of those four packages is in the dev's local run table (core, plugin-security, plugin-auth, spec, platform-objects, runtime, rest, objectql, cloud-connection, hono, sharing, approvals, automation, settings, datasource, storage, organizations, crm, showcase), and `dispatch-gates --ran 126/126` covers gate families, not those suites. Each of the four consumes `resolveUserAuthzGrants` through its own engine doubles or a booted app, the exact class this PR repaired in ten other packages by binding a catalog, so the red is read as this diff's until the shards say otherwise, not as flake. `Check Changeset`, `Spec property liveness`, `Build Docs`, `Dogfood Verify CLI` are `success`; `Console Pin Gate` and the packed-tarball smoke are roster skips.

### ① Derived judgments

Accept-set and public-surface changes the diff implies, each judged:

1. **`PositionSchema.permissionSets`** (`spec/src/identity/position.zod.ts`): `z.array(SnakeCaseIdentifierSchema).optional()`, and the closed-shape `guidance.permissionSets` refusal is deleted, not left beside it — **right** (#22006 B, #22601 B, the DRIFTED correction 6018622568; the field and its only reader land together). The `permissions` guidance and `PermissionSetSchema`'s `profiles` guidance now point at `permissionSets` — right. Pins: accepted list, snake_case refusal at `permissionSets.0` with no `unrecognized_keys` issue.
2. **Generated carriers of that key**: `authorable-surface/identity.json`, `liveness/position.json` (row `live`, evidence `resolve-authz-context.ts#positionSetNamesOf`), `state-counts/position.md` 12 → 13, `references/identity/position.mdx`, `package-api-assembled.mdx`, the position form (`tags` row) and the four metadata-form bundles with zh-CN / ja-JP / es-ES values, echo-decision count 668 → 669 — **right**, and the spec gates in `TypeScript Type Check` are green on them.
3. **ADR-0087 semantic entry `position-permission-sets-declared`** (entries file + `registry.ts` step 18) with surface, replacement, reason and acceptance criteria; the changeset carries the `registered` disposition marker — **right**: a runtime narrowing with an authorable key added is the registered shape, and the stored-row conversion is data (never a chain step), stated as such.
4. **`@objectstack/core` public surface widens**: `bindSecurityCatalogReader`, `securityCatalogReaderOf` (WeakMap keyed by engine and by its registry), `convertPositionBindingRows`, `convertDeactivatedCatalogRows` and their types — **right**, all named in the changeset; both conversions are pure, pinned (7 cases: order, declared-plus-added, same-binding-per-organization collapses, differing-per-organization is `conflicting` with the empty-binding organization included, dangling, ledger rows, conflicting flags) and wired into no boot path.
5. **`ADMIN_STANDING_SURFACE` / `ADMIN_STANDING_NON_TABLE_INPUTS`** (core, exported): the `sys_permission_set`, `sys_position`, `sys_position_permission_set` tables leave, `sys_metadata_activation` (`metadata_type`, `name`, `active`, role `derives`) enters, and the `kind` union gains `security-catalog` with the `admin_full_access` definition as a non-table input — **right in substance** (the surface must equal what the resolver reads; `admin-standing-surface.test.ts` observes the columns), **under-named**: the core paragraph of the changeset does not name this exported map's key change. Patch-round item.
6. **The resolver** (`resolve-authz-context.ts`): §6a reads each held position's definition by name and grants what `permissionSets` names; §6/§6b take every set body from the catalog; the `sys_position_permission_set` read, the by-id `sys_permission_set` read, the by-name set-row reads and the `sys_position` read are deleted; ONE `sys_metadata_activation` read (types `position`/`permission`, keyed by every name the resolution may grant, limit two rows a name) decides deactivation, and `ledgerUnregistered` asks the registry first so a composition without the ledger object issues no read (pinned, with the registered control). Platform standing is unchanged in shape (organization-less grant, `admin_full_access` resolved in the catalog, not switched off, anchor not retired). **Right** per the stage plan's row 1 and the ADR-0131 D3/D4 and ADR-0126 §4 text; no row fallback, no id bridge, no dual source. Golden: all 11 fixtures byte-identical on `grants`, legs 4 → 2 for the two position-bound fixtures, the recorded query moves written in the header; `request-grants-memo` and `session-grants-resolved-once` round-trip counts 10 → 6 / 8 → 6 follow from it. Note: `GRANTS_CACHE_WATCHED_OBJECTS` gains the ledger (right) and still watches the three tables the resolver no longer reads (harmless over-invalidation; a later stage trims it).
7. **The S5a and #20515 pins rewritten to the stage-1 rule** (a row-only set confers nothing, to its own organization too; an organization's junction row binds nothing, to its own members too; a catalog row's `active: false` is not read) — **right**, and each is the #15196 Q3 = A ruling applied; `explain-enforce-parity`'s `NOTES` column and `packages-orgless-grants-capability-gate`'s former control flip accordingly, with the reason written in.
8. **`plugin-security`**: the catalog is bound at `start()` with a loud `warn` on failure; the built-in `everyone` declares the baseline (`isDefault` set + `member_default`) in `permissionSets` at `kernel:ready` under the same #18535 high-privilege check (pinned beside the junction binding it mirrors); the `bindBaselineToEveryone` closure is untouched (batch #310 item 4 holds; 6a deletes it); the name-fold remedy text names the definition; `position-write-through` carries the stored definition's `permissionSets` through a row edit and a rename (pinned, ablated) — **right**. The write-through is not on item 4's list (seeders, projector, per-organization catalog), so the carry is a permitted correctness fix in a module 7b deletes. One recorded move under a wall: `everyone` now also names the organization-less `member_default` (`builtin-positions.boot` golden); accepted on the stated ground that the set carries no system or tab permission and enforcement already applied it additively (ADR-0090 D5).
9. **`plugin-auth`** (a declared deviation from the claim's "no plugin-auth" exclusion): `STANDING_KEYS_BY_TABLE` swaps `sys_permission_set` for the ledger, `refuseLedgerSwitchingAdminOff` refuses outright a ledger write switching `admin_full_access` off (fail-closed on an unreadable target row; a position, another set, a flow or switching it on pass with no read — pinned), registered as `beforeInsert`/`beforeUpdate` hooks on the ledger; the `sys_permission_set` hooks, the enumeration and the row-`active` diagnostic are untouched — **right as the minimum the correspondence gate forces** once item 5 changes; see ③.
10. **Examples**: the eleven personas declare `permissionSets`; both junction binders are kept with equality pins (`position-bindings.test.ts`, `inert-wirings.test.ts`) — **right**: the stage-2 readers (delegated-admin gate, explainer, sharing recipients) still read the junction, and the dispatch left the binder's fate to the dev's measured call.
11. **Test scaffolding**: ten per-package `security-catalog.testkit.ts` copies (nine byte-identical by content hash; core's and plugin-security's carry more) binding a catalog the fixtures' own rows convert to through the upgrade ceremony's conversion, and `ledgerFromTables` for the `active: false` rows — right as the no-cross-package-import shape, and it is what makes the equivalence claim mean something.
12. **Scope**: no governed surface in the file list, nothing under `content/docs/releases/`, no row deleted, no table dropped, no transition piece. The PR is a draft, `Part of #15204`, assignee `marchtian`.

### ② Semver level

Changeset `.changeset/15204-s1-position-permission-sets.md`: `@objectstack/spec`, `@objectstack/core`, `@objectstack/plugin-security`, `@objectstack/plugin-auth` at **`minor`**, body marked BREAKING with FROM → TO (junction rows → `permissionSets` on the definition, the one-line fix, the metadata-door path, the ceremony for stored rows, the Setup deactivation and binding gaps, the walled row-only loss and its promotion path) and the ADR-0087 disposition `registered position-permission-sets-declared` whose entry exists in the registry. `Clause-②: yes` on the PR body's second line and in the changeset; it matches the claim (6095611212) and the diff: a published accept set widens (`PositionSchema` accepts a key it refused). No arm is written; the accept-set movement is a widening, so no arm is the permitted spelling, and the runtime narrowing is carried by the bang plus the disposition, not by an arm. `minor` for a breaking change is the level the `Check Changeset` gate accepted on this head (the no-major gate the lane runs), so the level matches what the diff publishes. Gap, not a verdict carrier: the core paragraph should name the `ADMIN_STANDING_SURFACE` key change (①.5). The `!` title and the four packages named agree with the diff.

Clause-②: yes

### ③ Boundary flags

Every dev flag and `open_questions` entry from report 6101432403 and the PR body:

- **Q1, the D12 delegated-admin gate reads the junction until stage 2** (`setsBoundToPosition`, containment and the assignable-positions listing): **A, answered** — stage 2 lands before any release cut that contains this PR; nothing is fenced here (the no-transition-piece rule). The example personas keep their rows and are unaffected. Landing condition recorded for the epic PM.
- **Q2, deactivation at upgrade**: a position or set an organization deactivated in Setup (row `active`) grants again until C7b applies `convertDeactivatedCatalogRows`, and no door writes the ledger for `permission`/`position`, so Setup's Deactivate switches nothing off from this PR on. **A, with an escalation.** The read side is what the stage-0 text (6095755866) and ADR-0131 D3/D6 with ADR-0126 §4 place in the ledger, and stage 0 already assigns the write side ("the enable/disable actions for these two types") to stage 2 if they refuse the types — the dev measured that they do. What this PR adds is a window in which a visible Setup action silently stops working; the changeset and the PR body say so. The release-cut gate on C7b plus a ledger door for the two types is the epic PM's and the maintainer's to record on the card before any cut, and the stage-2 dispatch should carry the door. ⛔ Not a reason to re-open the row fallback (option B), which #22601 B forbids.
- **Q3, Setup's position page and the suggestion confirm still write junction rows that grant nothing until C9 + stage 7**: **A, answered** — documented in the changeset and the ADR-0087 entry; no write-through or projector (Zone 1).
- **Q4, size 3,776 changed lines over the 3,000 line**: **A, answered** — the nine helper copies are the no-cross-package-import shape, and a `./testing` subpath on `@objectstack/core` is a published-surface decision of its own. Consequence for landing: AGENTS.md Multi-agent discipline §7 class (c) applies, so this PR lands only on an authorized APPROVED review and the owning seat, or a human merge; this record does not substitute for that approval. Batch #310 item 7 asks that such a PR be named with its size; the body's first paragraph does so.
- **Q5, the plugin-auth deviation**: **A now, B in stage 2b** — the flat ledger refusal cannot be talked past and refuses more, never less; stage 2b (6095755866, order correction 4) reworks the guard's 18 `PERMISSION_SET` sites and its enumeration onto the ledger and drops the flat refusal then.
- **Deviations stated in the body** (ten packages' fake engines bound to a catalog; the S5a/#20515 pin rewrites; `cloud-connection` fixtures answering the ledger empty; the form-bundle regeneration and the three translations; the #18535 registry `_packageId` stamp after the second `main` merge; the explain harness gaining a registry): each is a mechanical consequence of the reader switch, read against the diff — accepted. The `position-write-through` carry: accepted (①.8).
- **Out-of-scope findings** (`check:platform-checklist` red on `main`; the explainer's row-based "deactivated" label; the last-admin enumeration's row `active`): carriers named (none / stage 2 / stage 2b), nothing to answer here.
- **Flag raised by this review**: the four packages whose CI suites are red were not in the dev's verification table, and the body's claim "CI runs them on the head" is now answered by CI: red. The patch round owes the four shards green, with the same catalog-binding treatment where the cause is the fake-engine class, and a measured reason where it is not (the dogfood shard boots real apps, so a red there may be a behavioural regression, not a harness one, and must be read before it is "fixed").

Why FAIL: two of the seven required contexts are `failure` on this head (`Test Core`, `Dogfood Regression Gate`). The contract judgments above hold; a PASS record is owed on a head where those shards are green, with ①.5's changeset sentence added and ③ Q2's release-cut condition recorded on the card.
